gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-pahaw: Loose, rope-like lettering with a ballpoint feel up top. Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong has the plain sans job, with a tall lowercase and gapped rounds, while Delius Unicase does the talking with big, relaxed strokes.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-palmy: Delius Unicase draws every stem and tail like bent rope. Noto Sans Palmyrene takes the quieter job, with curves that stop short and compact ascenders, while the heading handles the friendly, handmade emphasis.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-pau-c: Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau keeps its curves open and its capitals low. Delius Unicase, with its pronounced x-height and uniform pen line, makes the handwritten counterpoint above it.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-phags: Relaxed, with a pen that never changes pressure. Noto Sans PhagsPa then does what the heading can't, offering see-through openings and a gentle step up to capitals, while Delius Unicase supplies the warmth.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-phoen: Noto Sans Phoenician reads modern and tall, with s curves flung wide at both ends. Delius Unicase brings the bent-paperclip handwriting, and the sans keeps everything below it generous and easy to follow.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-psalt: Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi sits low and approachable. Delius Unicase earns its keep big and short, where its swell-free handwritten strokes and rope-ladder spacing can be seen.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-rejan: Stitched-thread handwriting meets a body with wide, porthole-like counters. Delius Unicase belongs large and brief, in headings.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-runic: Noto Sans Runic reads big and tight, its curves never closing back on themselves, under a heading drawn like bent tubing. Handmade warmth against crisp sans.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-samar: Delius Unicase draws every curve without stress, like a single steady pen line bent into letters. Its looseness against Noto Sans Samaritan's hefty, daylight-filled lowercase.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-saura: Friendly handwriting, one line weight throughout. Delius Unicase is best at greeting with big, inviting strokes, while Noto Sans Saurashtra quietly carries the text with connected counters and barely taller capitals.
